work.headingAccent: From one business task to an application your team can control.
work.s1Desc: aiNOW identifies what starts the task, who approves it, and what result the customer or employee should receive.
work.s2Desc: aiNOW reviews the information, permissions, exceptions, and systems already used by the business.
work.s3Desc: The proposal states what the application will do, what stays manual, when it will be ready, and the expected monthly cost.
work.s4Desc: The application is checked on common requests, missing information, sensitive data, and cases that need a person.
work.s5Desc: Actions that need permission wait for an employee. Safe routine actions continue automatically.
work.s6Desc: Your team receives the application and the information needed to run it. Ongoing support remains optional.

faq.subtitle: Short answers about the work, safety, cost, and ownership.
faq.a1: A working application for one agreed business task, plus the checks, access, documents, and handover needed to use it.
faq.q2: How is the monthly cost estimated?
faq.a2: aiNOW estimates it from request volume, the number of steps, and the services required. The final estimate is agreed before development.
faq.a3: aiNOW prepares realistic business situations and confirms the expected action for each one before customers use the application.
faq.q4: What happens when the application is unsure?
faq.a4: It can pause, ask for missing information, or send the case to an employee instead of guessing.
faq.a5: That depends on the services selected. aiNOW documents the route and access before launch, including any required region or private environment.
faq.q6: What if the task is still unclear?
faq.a6: The audit maps the task, the exceptions, the people involved, and the useful result before a build is proposed.
faq.q7: Is the audit fee credited to the build?
faq.a7: Yes. The full audit fee is deducted from the agreed build price.
faq.a8: aiNOW shows the effect on price and timing before the added work starts.
faq.q9: Can an internal team build the first version?
faq.a9: Yes. aiAPP is useful when the application must also be checked, launched, documented, and handed over for daily use.
faq.q10: Can aiAPP build a normal business application?
faq.a10: Yes, when the application includes automated decisions, customer replies, document work, or connections to existing systems.
faq.a11: No public case studies are claimed here. The paid audit is the small first step for checking the approach on your process.
faq.q12: Does aiNOW hold SOC 2 or ISO certification?
faq.a12: Not currently. If procurement requires a specific certificate, that boundary is confirmed before work begins.
faq.q13: Can it connect to existing systems?
faq.a13: Often yes. The audit confirms available access and shows any limitation before the integration is included in scope.
faq.a14: aiAPP builds a new application. vibecoding.ge checks and repairs an application that already exists.

eval.heading: What work will the application do?
eval.subtitle: See how the same application handles ordinary requests, missing information, sensitive data, and cases that need a person.
eval.c1: A customer asks where an order is
eval.c3: The delivery address must be changed
eval.c4: A customer asks for private account data
eval.c5: The answer is ready to send
eval.outcome: The application knows when to act, when to ask, and when to stop.
eval.note: These are example situations. aiNOW prepares the real list from your process before launch.

trace.heading: How does aiNOW check it before a customer sees it?
trace.subtitle: A visible four-step path shows what enters, what is checked, what action is allowed, and what the customer receives.
trace.safetyCheckDetail: The order belongs to this customer and may be shown.
trace.actionDetail: The application reads the current delivery status.
trace.customerResultDetail: The verified delivery update is ready.
trace.outcome: Nothing is sent until the request and the allowed action have been checked.

handoff.heading: What stays under your control?
handoff.subtitle: The handover is visible: code, access, service accounts, documents, and operating control move to your team.
handoff.outcome: Your team receives every item needed to operate the application.

cost.heading: What will it cost each month?
cost.subtitle: Change the expected request volume, the work per request, and the processing level. The example updates immediately.
cost.result: The real number is agreed before development
cost.note: This example is not a quote. aiNOW calculates the estimate from the selected services and your expected use.

ladder.heading: Start small, then choose the next step.
ladder.subtitle: Open any step. The audit comes first; development and ongoing support are separate decisions.
ladder.r1what: aiNOW maps the task, checks the systems and exceptions, and gives a scope, date, and monthly estimate.
ladder.r1risk: If there is no useful build, the report still explains the finding and the next practical option.
ladder.r2what: aiNOW builds the agreed application, checks the business situations, and prepares the handover.
ladder.r2risk: The full audit fee is deducted from the build price.
ladder.r3what: aiNOW can monitor costs, maintain connections, and help the team after launch.
ladder.r3risk: Support is optional because the code, access, documents, and control remain with the client.
ladder.note: Each step has its own scope, price, and decision.
